pr_title: Return error on no-browser option if repo don't exists
pr_body:

Fixes #7255 

```
repo doesn't exists, return non-zero error
❯❯ ./bin/gh browse -n -R kousikmitra/unknown
github.com/kousikmitra/unknown doesn't exists

public repo
❯❯ ./bin/gh browse -n -R kousikmitra/cli
https://github.com/kousikmitra/cli

private repo
❯❯ ./bin/gh browse -n -R kousikmitra/.config
https://github.com/kousikmitra/.config
```
pr_comments: In case `-n` is not specified, this will still open the browser and show 404 page, should we handle that also? So that if the repo doesn't exists we can avoid opening browser.

> In case -n is not specified, this will still open the browser and show 404 page, should we handle that also? So that if the repo doesn't exists we can avoid opening browser.

I think it's fine to leave this as-is.

@vilmibm @kousikmitra Is there a reason why we are not testing the full URL that is generated and instead just checking the the repo exists? Feels like we could make this more accurate by making a HEAD request to the generated URL instead.

issue_context.title: `gh browse -n -R` should error on 404
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

If a target repo does not exist, eg: `gh browse -R cli/cli` brings up a 404 in the browser, but  `gh browse -n -R cli/cli` returns a destination URL that does not exist and exit status 0.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior
```
$  gh browse -n -R cli/cli
https://github.com/cli/cli

$ echo $?
0

$  gh browse -n -R cli/cli-doesnotexist
https://github.com/cli/cli-doesnotexist

$ echo $?
0
```
### Expected vs actual behavior

Expect to test if the constructed destination URL exist before displaying to the user, or at least provide a warning that it's not reachable.
`gh browse -n -R ORG/REPO` where ORG/REPO does not exist should return error message and non-zero exit code

Maybe 2 error codes - one if ORG reachable but REPO is not, one for ORG/REPO not reachable?

### Logs
See steps to reproduce
comments:
I'm fine with a check to ensure that the repo we're about to open a page for actually exists. It means a network call when there previously wasn't one but i think that's acceptable.

To keep it simple, just a single non-zero error code for `owner/repo` not existing is sufficient for now.
